issues.legal_issue: The abatement of an appeal concerning one claimant does not require dismissal of the entire appeal when the claims are distinct and severable and the remaining relief can be granted without producing unenforceable or contradictory decrees.
material_facts: The proceedings concerned the apportionment of compensation among numerous claimants asserting distinct shares in acquired land.
The claimants’ individual claims were combined and decided together because they raised similar issues, but each claimant could have pursued a separate claim and appeal without joining the others.
Five appellants died during the appeals, and their legal representatives were not brought on record within time.
The claims of the remaining appellants were independent, and a decision on those claims could be enforced without negating a decree concerning a deceased appellant.
issues.conclusion: The appeals did not abate in their entirety because of the deaths and non-substitution of the five appellants; they could proceed on the merits for the remaining claimants.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 22 of the Code of Civil Procedure, abatement as to one party does not automatically abate an appeal as to others. Whether the remaining appeal can proceed depends on the nature of the rights and relief and whether a decree for the remaining parties would be unenforceable or mutually destructive of a decree that has become final. The Court applied the principles in Nathu Ram v. State of Punjab, Ram Sarup v. Munshi, Harihar Prasad Singh v. Balmiki Prasad Singh, and Indian Oxygen Ltd. v. Ram Adhar Singh. It also relied on Sections 11, 18, 30 and 31 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, concerning awards, references and apportionment, and held that consolidated adjudication of distinct compensation claims does not by itself make them a joint and inseverable claim.

predicates.appeal_from_consolidated_multi_claim_adj: The proceeding is an appeal from a decision that dealt together with claims made by multiple claimants.
predicates.claimants_hold_independent_severable_rig: Each claimant asserts an individual right that can be decided without determining or impairing the rights of the other claimants.
predicates.one_party_dies_without_substitution: A party to the appeal dies and that party’s legal representatives are not brought on record in time.
predicates.remaining_relief_can_be_enforced_without: Relief for the remaining parties can be enforced without negating or making unenforceable a decree concerning the deceased party.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns consolidated claims based on independent rights, a party’s death without timely substitution does not prevent the remaining appeal from proceeding if relief for the remaining parties can be enforced without conflict.

issues.legal_issue: A court should take a liberal and justice-oriented approach to delay in substituting a deceased claimant’s legal representatives when rejecting the application would foreclose adjudication of other claimants’ independent rights.
material_facts: The appeals involved multiple appellants asserting distinct and independent claims.
Five appellants died during the proceedings, and applications to bring their legal representatives on record were filed late.
The High Court rejected the applications and dismissed the appeals in their entirety, thereby preventing the surviving appellants’ claims from being decided on the merits.
The Supreme Court held that the delay should have been condoned and directed that the deceased appellants’ legal representatives be brought on record.
issues.conclusion: The rejection of the substitution and delay-condonation applications was set aside, and the legal representatives were directed to be brought on record.
issues.legal_principle: Order 22 of the Code of Civil Procedure is a procedural mechanism to facilitate effective adjudication, not a rigid device for defeating substantial rights. Procedural law is the handmaid of justice, and courts should adopt a liberal and reasonable approach to condonation of delay where a strict approach would unjustly foreclose adjudication on the merits. The Court relied on the independent-rights principles in Harihar Prasad Singh v. Balmiki Prasad Singh and Indian Oxygen Ltd. v. Ram Adhar Singh.

predicates.appeal_from_multi_claim_adjudication: The proceeding is an appeal involving claims by multiple parties that were dealt with together.
predicates.remaining_claimants_hold_independent_rig: The claimants whose appeals remain have rights that can be adjudicated independently of the deceased party’s rights.
predicates.substitution_application_is_delayed: An application to substitute the legal representatives of a deceased party is filed after the applicable time limit.
predicates.refusing_substitution_would_foreclose_me: Refusing substitution would prevent the remaining claimants from obtaining adjudication of their independent claims on the merits.

issues.definition: When an appeal involves independently held claims, delay in substitution should be excused if refusing substitution would prevent the remaining claimants from having their claims decided on the merits.

issues.legal_issue: A person claiming an interest in compensation may be denied impleadment at the appellate stage where that person’s predecessor was not a party to the proceedings before the lower courts and the application is made after the hearing has concluded.
material_facts: After the hearing had concluded and orders had been reserved, persons claiming through a deceased person sought to be impleaded as interested in the compensation.
The deceased predecessor had not been a party before either the Reference Court or the High Court.
The Supreme Court rejected the applications to be impleaded.
issues.conclusion: The applications for impleadment were rejected because the applicants’ predecessor had not been a party at any stage before the lower courts.
issues.legal_principle: The Court found no justification for entertaining the applicants’ claim to come on record at that stage because their predecessor had not been a party to the proceedings before the courts below.

predicates.appellate_proceeding_after_hearing_concl: The proceeding is an appeal in which the hearing has concluded and the court has reserved its decision.
predicates.proposed_party_claims_through_predecesso: A person seeks to be added to the appeal on the basis of an interest claimed through a predecessor.
predicates.predecessor_was_not_party_before_lower_c: The predecessor through whom the proposed party claims was not a party to the proceedings before the lower courts.

issues.definition: A court may reject a post-hearing request to join an appeal when the proposed party claims through someone who was not a party before the lower courts.
